text:
maria: seeing a spike in GPU provisioning failures in us-west2-az3 this morning, looks tied to a subset of nodes going into ReadOnly and slow attach times

sam: saw that too — large queue of pending pods, autoscaler couldn't fill because many nodes reported 'device write errors'

jin: initial dig — not classic nvme wear. IOPS await and fsync latency skyrocket around the same times as kubelet tear-downs. suspect metadata churn from containerd/overlayfs lowerdir churn causing tiny syncs.

maria: logs? any correlation with cron jobs or maintenance?

jin: paste of iostat snapshot from one affected host:
```
Device            r/s     w/s   rkB/s   wkB/s  await  svctm  %util
nvme0n1         120.0  980.0   512.0  2048.0  45.8   1.02  99.8
```
and dstat showed thousands of small write syscalls. also found containerd bolt DB fsync bursts: /var/lib/containerd/io.containerd.metadata.v1.bolt/meta.db

ashley: infra-bot posted a correlation alert at 08:12:56 for kubelet restart + overlay unmount failures :infra-bot:  
infra-bot: "us-west2-az3 nodes: 12 overlayfs unmount error; 9 reported high fsync latency"

sam: are these nodes running our ephemeral job runner workload? that does heavy small-file writes (checkpointing).

jin: yes, and we found logrotate and our checkpointer both running at 08:10 window. combined they generate a fsync storm. overlayfs lowerdir means each small write hits metacopy and causes metadata syncs. result: per-queue starvation and NVMe queue depth spike -> device flapping to ro.

maria: any quick mitigations to get provisioning back up?

jin: 1) throttle checkpointer frequency (set env CHECKPOINT_FREQ=60s) on the job runner DaemonSet. 2) temporarily pause logrotate on /var/lib/containerd by adding a local override to 24h. 3) set kernel overlay unmount retry to longer to avoid kubelet racing (sysctl tweak). 4) cordon+drain affected nodes one-by-one and force node reboot to clear overlay lowerdir leaks — but that is intrusive.

ashley: can we AVAIL add a fallback routing so autoscaler uses eu-central spare capacity until this is fixed? swapping regions will bump cost but buys time.

sam: yes, I'll open a short-lived autoscaler policy to allow spillover to eu-central for the next 3 hours. :thumbsup:

maria: Jin — can you attach the smartctl / nvme-cli output? want to rule out firmware bug.

jin: smart looks fine, wear_level 4% used. nvme logs show no panic. attaching snippet:
```
$ nvme smart-log /dev/nvme0n1
critical_warning  : 0
temperature       : 38 C
percentage_used   : 4
media_errors      : 0
```

jin: conclusion: not media wear but sustained fsync storms + metadata write amplification on overlayfs + containerd bolt DB causing IOPS exhaustion.

maria: okay plan: jin/ashley to push mitigations (checkpoint throttle + logrotate override) ASAP, sam to enable cross-region spillover, i'll schedule rolling reboots for the 12 affected nodes in small batches. open ticket for storage team to explore overlayfs metadata path optimizations and maybe move bolt DB to tmpfs for runners.

ashley: creating an incident ticket now with runbook steps and mitigation commands. pinging storage team.

infra-bot: incident created: INC-2026-1543 - "us-west2-az3 overlayfs fsync storm -> nvme ro"

sam: rolling autoscaler policy in place, starting drain+reboot on node-uw2-az3-07 now.

maria: keep updates here, if anything shows persistent nvme errors escalate to hw-swap. thanks everyone.
